item.title: Why are we doing this?
item.description:
Why are we doing this? #

One page, before any terminal.

You can now build real software by describing it — what people call vibe coding: you say what you want, a model writes it, you steer. It works, startlingly well. And it has a failure mode everyone who tries it eventually hits: three weeks in, neither you nor the model remembers why anything is the way it is. The code is there; the reasoning evaporated with the chat window it happened in.

item.title: Chapter 2 — Setting up your tools
item.description:
Chapter 2 — Setting up your tools #

macOS path. Windows readers: tentative notes are marked — we haven’t walked them end-to-end yet, and we’d genuinely value your corrections ( open an issue with the step ID). Budget 25–40 minutes, mostly waiting on installers.

Each tool below comes with its why — not as filler, but because “install these five things” with no reasons is exactly the context-free instruction style this whole methodology exists to replace.

item.title: Chapter 3 — Your first project
item.description:
Chapter 3 — Your first project #

A real project: a Wordle variant, live on GitHub Pages, built with a model collaborator — and your first decisions on the record. Budget 45–60 minutes. One path; each step says how to verify it worked.

A GitHub account ☰
GitHub is where your project’s code, its decision records, and (in a few steps) its live website all live. If you already have an account, skip to P2.

Go to github.com/signup. Don’t stall on the username — you can change it later (Settings → Account), add or swap email addresses, all of it. Pick something and move.
